items.h: A clock shows the time.

items.s: I love hot ___ on a cold day.
items.h: Say it slowly: choc-o-late. Don't forget the o!

items.s: Mum told me to ___ my coat on.
items.h: After to, use the plain word: to put my coat on.

items.s: I hope we win the game and don't ___.
items.h: Lose is the opposite of win. Loose means not tight.

items.s: Last night I ___ a book about the planets.
items.h: Read looks the same in the past, but it sounds like red.

items.s: I need a new ___ of shoes.
items.h: A pair means two that go together. A pear is a fruit.

items.s: We ate juicy red ___ for pudding.
items.h: Cherry changes y to i and adds -es: cherries.

items.s: Look at that bird! ___ is so pretty.
items.h: Use it for an animal or a thing: it is pretty.

items.s: ___ your rabbit like carrots?
items.h: One rabbit, so we ask with does.

items.s: Have you got ___ brothers or sisters?
items.h: In questions, we often use any: any brothers?

items.s: This box is full ___ toys.
items.h: We say full of: the box is full of toys.

items.s: A ___ has a long neck and eats leaves from trees.
items.h: A giraffe's long neck helps it reach tall trees.

items.s: We borrowed books from the ___.
items.h: Library has two r's: lib-rar-y.

items.s: I want to ___ an astronaut one day.
items.h: After want to, use be: I want to be an astronaut.

items.s: Yesterday I ___ the ball with one hand!
items.h: Catch changes to caught in the past, not catched.

items.s: There are ___ planets in our solar system.
items.h: Eight is the number 8. Ate is the past of eat.

items.s: My sister likes to sing ___ dance.
items.h: And joins two things she likes doing.

items.s: My toast is hot, but my ice lolly is ___.
items.h: Cold is the opposite of hot.

items.s: Dad washed all the ___ after tea.
items.h: Words ending in sh add -es: dish, dishes.

items.s: The teacher asked ___ to sit down.
items.h: After asked, use us, not we: she asked us.

items.s: My brother ___ his homework after tea.
items.h: One person takes does: he does his homework.

items.s: We use a ___ to brush our teeth.
items.h: A toothbrush cleans our teeth.

items.s: Have you had ___ to eat?
items.h: Enough ends in -ough, which sounds like uff.

items.s: I ___ going to bake a cake tomorrow.
items.h: With I, we say am: I am going to bake.

items.s: Last Friday I ___ a whole length of the pool.
items.h: Swim changes to swam in the past: I swam a length.

items.s: I got a ___ bike for my birthday.
items.h: New means not old. Knew is the past of know.

items.s: We didn't see ___ birds today.
items.h: After didn't, we use any: we didn't see any.

items.s: I put all my toys away, so my room is ___.
items.h: Tidy is the opposite of messy.

items.s: We made ham ___ for the picnic.
items.h: Words ending in ch add -es: sandwich, sandwiches.

items.s: Lily and Max fed ___ goldfish.
items.h: Their means belonging to them: their goldfish.

items.s: ___ you like chocolate ice cream?
items.h: With you, we ask with do: do you like it?

items.s: The ___ goes round the Earth and shines at night.
items.h: The moon goes round the Earth. We see it at night.

items.s: Mum is very ___ today.
items.h: Busy is spelt with a u, but it sounds like bizzy.

items.s: I hopped and ___ all the way home.
items.h: Skip doubles its p before -ed: skipped.

items.s: Last winter the pond ___ solid.
items.h: Freeze changes to froze in the past, not freezed.

items.s: There are seven days in a ___.
items.h: A week is seven days. Weak means not strong.

items.s: I was born ___ 2018.
items.h: Use in with years: I was born in 2018.

items.s: The shop was closed, ___ we went home.
items.h: So tells us what we did next.

items.s: Are there ___ biscuits in the tin?
items.h: In questions, we often use any: are there any?

items.s: Daytime is light, but night-time is ___.
items.h: Dark is the opposite of light.

items.s: Two big ___ stopped outside our school.
items.h: Words ending in s add -es: bus, buses.

items.s: ___ coat is this on the floor?
items.h: Whose asks who something belongs to: whose coat?

items.s: My cats ___ not like the rain.
items.h: Cats means more than one, so we say do not.

items.s: A group of sheep is called a ___.
items.h: A group of sheep or birds is called a flock.

items.s: ___ is your name?
items.h: What starts with wh, just like when and where.

items.s: Yesterday it ___ all day long.
items.h: Add -ed for the past: yesterday it rained.

items.s: I ___ my new red hat to school yesterday.
items.h: Wear changes to wore in the past, not weared.

items.s: ___ raining, so take a coat.
items.h: It's is short for it is: it is raining.
